beats.say: Sometimes someone inside wants to take data on purpose. Knowing the signs matters.
Asking for someone else's password and interest in files outside one's job are serious warning signs.

body.text: Give me your password, I will grab a few folders from the archive.

beats.say: But do not investigate yourself, accuse or spread rumours. One sign is not proof of guilt.
Report what you saw to the security team in confidence. Specialists will check the rest.

scenes.title: Messages from colleagues
scenes.intro: It is evening and messages from colleagues arrive on your phone. Choose the right reply to each.

body.text: Hi, they closed my access by mistake.
Give me your password, I will take the project folders from the archive and return it tomorrow.

actions.label: Send the password
actions.feedback: Everything done with your password is logged in your name. Never give it to anyone, colleagues included.

actions.label: I cannot give my password, contact IT support
actions.feedback: Right. If access was closed, only IT and the manager can sort it out.

body.text: Fine. Then copy the folders to a USB stick, I will pick it up tonight.
I will need them at my new job.

actions.label: OK, I will copy them
actions.feedback: Your organisation's data does not go to another job. Copying it makes you part of the leak.

actions.label: No, I cannot do that
actions.feedback: Right, a calm short no is enough. Now tell the security team.

body.text: Leyla: I saw Tural in the archive at night. Let's check his computer and then tell everyone.

actions.label: Agreed, let's check
actions.feedback: Checking on your own can spoil evidence and damage an innocent person.

actions.label: Not in the group. Let's report what we saw to security in confidence
actions.feedback: Right. The facts go to the right channel and no rumour starts.

body.text: Thank you. Please do not discuss this with colleagues, we will contact you if needed.

actions.label: Reply: understood
actions.feedback: Right. Confidentiality protects both the inquiry and your colleague.

actions.label: Forward to the department group
actions.feedback: Spreading the report harms the inquiry and can unfairly hurt your colleague.

question.prompt: Which ones are serious warning signs?

options.label: Asking for access to systems outside one's job
options.feedback: Right. Interest in access that is not needed deserves attention.

options.label: Asking for someone else's password
options.feedback: Right. Someone with proper access does not need another person's password.

options.label: Copying many files to a personal USB stick or mail
options.feedback: Right. Data leaving the organisation is the clearest sign.

options.label: Sometimes working late
options.feedback: On its own this is normal: many people work late. One sign is no reason to accuse.

options.label: Asking many questions in meetings
options.feedback: That is interest in the work, not a threat.

scenes.explain: A sign is not an accusation, it is a reason to report. Specialists decide.

nodes.text: For a week Kamal has copied secret project files to a personal flash drive every evening. Once he said: "Nobody values me here."

choices.label: I report what I saw to security in confidence
choices.feedback: Right. You pass on facts, specialists draw conclusions.

choices.label: I ask him directly: why are you taking the files?
choices.feedback: An accusation causes conflict and may lead to traces being wiped. Leave it to specialists.

choices.label: I search his desk myself in the evening
choices.feedback: Searching on your own can break the rules and spoil evidence.

nodes.text: Thank you. Please write down what you saw, when and where.
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: Thank you. <breath> Please write down what you saw, when and where.

choices.label: I write only what I saw, with dates and times
choices.feedback: Great. Precise facts are the basis of a fair check.

choices.label: I also add my opinions about his character
choices.feedback: Guesswork can lead to an unfair result. Write only the facts you saw.

choices.label: I tell colleagues to keep away from him
choices.feedback: That is a rumour and can unfairly hurt your colleague. Only the security team should know.

scenes.prompt: You notice suspicious behaviour. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Stay calm and accuse no one
Note what you saw, with date and time
Report to the security team in confidence
Afterwards, do not discuss it with others

scenes.explain: You pass on the facts, the inquiry and decision belong to specialists. If your organisation names another channel, use it.

points: Never hand over your password or work data
Do not accuse and do not investigate yourself
Report the facts to security in confidence
